::: {#exm-bias-sample-mean}
#### Bias of two estimators of a mean

Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ each have expectation $\E{X_i} = \mu$,
as in @exm-estimator.
By @thm-bias-exprs,
the bias of the sample mean $\bar X$ is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bias{\bar X}
&= \E{\bar X} - \mu
&& \text{(bias equals expectation minus truth)}\\
&= \E{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i} - \mu
&& \text{(definition of $\bar X$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n}\E{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i} - \mu
&& \text{(factor the constant $\tfrac{1}{n}$ out of the expectation)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \E{X_i} - \mu
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \mu - \mu
&& \text{($\E{X_i} = \mu$ for every $i$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n} \cdot n\mu - \mu
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\mu$)}\\
&= \mu - \mu
&& \text{(cancel $n$)}\\
&= 0
&& \text{(subtract)}
\end{aligned}
$$

and the bias of the single-observation estimator $\hat\mu^{(2)} = X_1$ is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bias{X_1}
&= \E{X_1} - \mu
&& \text{(bias equals expectation minus truth)}\\
&= \mu - \mu
&& \text{($\E{X_1} = \mu$)}\\
&= 0
&& \text{(subtract)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So both estimators have zero bias,
even though $\bar X$ uses all $n$ observations and $X_1$ uses only one.

:::
